answers.questionRaw: PART 2 — PASSAGE COMPLETION Questions 13–17 Read the following passage and choose the letter A, B, C, or D to indicate the option that best fits each numbered blank. Twenty years ago, Hillcrest was a village outside the city. Most homes stood along a narrow road, while the nearest secondary school and hospital were several kilometres away. (13) ______. Reaching either facility involved a long walk followed by a bus ride. Hillcrest is now part of the expanding city. Since 2015, (14) ______. These developments have attracted families seeking larger homes outside the crowded centre. However, many adults still work in central districts, so they travel towards the city each morning. The main road has become busier. A direct bus now connects Hillcrest with the hospital, but its first departure is at nine. Morning appointments there begin at eight. (15) ______. For residents without cars, the new connection therefore has a practical limitation despite removing the need to change buses. A report also describes population trends. Between 2000 and 2020, the urban share of the region’s population rose from 30 to 45 per cent. Over the same period, the rural share fell from 70 to 55 per cent. In other words, (16) ______. These percentages describe how the population was distributed; they do not, by themselves, tell readers how many people lived in either area. Hillcrest’s development needs to be assessed through residents’ routines. For those with the earliest hospital appointments, (17) ______. Evaluating urban development involves checking how new services fit the needs of the people using them. Question 13.A. Residents could usually reach both facilities without leaving their own streetB.
